subproblems.title: The mass measure of a current on ℝ^P vanishes off the support of the current
subproblems.statement: Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (VO), the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose tsupport is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (a current on U = univ) and let μ be a measure on ℝ^P such that M_W(X) = μ(W) for every open set W ⊆ ℝ^P. Then μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0, i.e. μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0. Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → X.massOn W = μ W) → μ X.supportᶜ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (1d) of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition (used there for T and, in step 2, for ∂T); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928).
1. (The complement of the support is the open zero region.) By definition, spt X = ℝ^P \ Z with Z := X.zeroRegion, the union of all open W with compact closure (contained in ℝ^P) on which X vanishes. Hence (spt X)ᶜ = Z (the complement of univ \ Z is Z), and Z is open, being a union of open sets (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion).
2. By the hypothesis applied to the open set W := Z, μ((spt X)ᶜ) = μ(Z) = M_Z(X), and by definition M_Z(X) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) admissible for M_Z (tsupport ω ⊆ Z and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x).
3. Let ω be admissible for M_Z. Then tsupport ω ⊆ Z = (spt X)ᶜ, so tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X (Set.disjoint_of_subset_left with disjoint_compl_left). By (VO), applied with U := ℝ^P and S := X, X(ω) = 0, hence ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) = ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0.
4. Every element of the set whose supremum is M_Z(X) is therefore 0, so M_Z(X) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), i.e. M_Z(X) = 0. By step 2, μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: (spt X)ᶜ = X.zeroRegion, which is open (isOpen_zeroRegion).
μ((spt X)ᶜ) = M_Z(X), the supremum of ofReal X(ω) over ω admissible for Z = X.zeroRegion.
Every such ω has tsupport disjoint from spt X, so X(ω) = 0 by (VO).
The supremum is ≤ 0 (sSup_le), so μ((spt X)ᶜ) = 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 8 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition (the mass measure μ_T := R.measure and the integrality of the shells W_j); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928). Siblings used: null_off_support (cmcsd_sh_measure_compl_support_eq_zero) and IR = imrep_restriction (lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict: for every IMRep R in U, (a) R.measure ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier, (b) R.orient is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable, (c) for every Borel E and every IMRep R′ in U with R′.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient: R′.measure = R.measure⌞E and R′.action ω = ∫_E R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) for every form ω).
1. Since T is integer multiplicity, choose an IMRep R in ℝ^P (U = univ) representing T: T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Put μ := R.measure and ξ := R.orient.
2. ((5) and (1).) ℝ^P is open, so (MR) with U := ℝ^P gives M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, which is (5). For W := ℝ^P this gives μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(T) = M(T) < ∞ (T.mass is by definition T.massOn univ), so μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure.mk), which is (1).
3. ((2) and (3).) By IR (b), ξ = R.orient is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, which is (2). By (IMC)(d), for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x we have |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α. By IR (a), μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier, so every property holding Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. holds μ-a.e. (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le); this is (3).
4. ((4).) Apply IR (c) with the Borel set E := ℝ^P and R′ := R; its hypotheses R.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P (Set.inter_univ), R.mult = R.mult and R.orient = R.orient hold. It gives R.action ω = ∫_{ℝ^P} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (setIntegral_univ) for every form ω. Since R represents T, T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), which is (4).
5. ((6).) By step 2, M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, so the sibling null_off_support, applied with (VO), X := T and μ, gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0, which is (6).
6. ((7).) Let E be Borel and X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). By (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^P (open), R and E there are A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R′ with R′.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient (that R′ represents A is not needed). By IR (c) applied to E and R′, R′.action ω = ∫_E R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = X(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Hence R′ represents X, and X is integer multiplicity.
7. Steps 2–6 show that μ and ξ have properties (1)–(7). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose an IMRep R of T; μ := R.measure, ξ := R.orient.
(MR) gives M_W(T) = μ(W) for open W, hence μ(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞ and μ is finite.
IR (a), (b) and (IMC)(d) give a.e. strong measurability of ξ and the μ-a.e. bound |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|.
IR (c) with E = ℝ^P, R′ = R gives T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ.
null_off_support with (VO) gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0.
(IMC)(b) gives an IMRep R′ with carrier R.carrier ∩ E; IR (c) shows R′.action = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω), so X is IM.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 6, 7, 10(a)–(b), 11 and 13 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition, stated for a general current represented by a finite measure (the parent applies it to (T, μ_T, ξ, A_{r_j}, W_j) and to (∂T, μ_∂, ξ_∂, B_{r_j}, D_j)); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928). Sibling used: EB = eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn: if M_W(Z) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M_W(Z).toReal).
Notation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) put f_ω(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). Put E_0 := {x : r_0 ≤ d(x)} and E_{j+1} := {x : r_{j+1} ≤ d(x) ∧ d(x) < r_j}. As d is continuous, {d < t} is open, {t ≤ d} is closed, and all these sets are Borel (measurableSet_lt, measurableSet_le).
1. (Bound for a test form.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P). The map x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous: ω is smooth, hence continuous, and α ↦ |α| = √(Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})²) is continuous because each evaluation α ↦ α(v) is continuous (continuous_eval_const) and finite sums, squares and Real.sqrt are continuous. It vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω (|0| = 0, covectorEuclideanNorm_zero; HasCompactSupport.comp_left). Hence it is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is c_ω with |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω for every x, and c_ω ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0.
2. (Integrability.) f_ω is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, as the image of the pair (ξ, ω), with ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable and ω continuous, under the continuous evaluation map (L, α) ↦ L(α) (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ with isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). For μ-a.e. x, |f_ω(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω by the a.e. bound on ξ and step 1. As μ is finite, f_ω is μ-integrable (Integrable.of_bound), hence integrable on every set.
3. ((a) Shell integrals.) j = 0: {d < r_0}ᶜ = {r_0 ≤ d} = E_0, so by integral_add_compl (step 2) Y_0(ω) = X(ω) − A_0(ω) = ∫ f_ω dμ − ∫_{d<r_0} f_ω dμ = ∫_{E_0} f_ω dμ. j + 1: as r_{j+1} < r_j, {d < r_{j+1}} ⊆ {d < r_j}, and {d < r_j} \ {d < r_{j+1}} = {r_{j+1} ≤ d ∧ d < r_j} = E_{j+1}; so by setIntegral_sdiff (step 2) Y_{j+1}(ω) = ∫_{d<r_j} f_ω dμ − ∫_{d<r_{j+1}} f_ω dμ = ∫_{E_{j+1}} f_ω dμ. This is (a); thus Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} f_ω dμ for every j.
4. (Shell geometry.) E_j ⊆ {r_j ≤ d} for every j. If i < j then j = j′ + 1 with j′ ≥ i, and E_j ⊆ {d < r_{j′}} ⊆ {d < r_i} since r is decreasing. Hence for i < j no x lies in E_i ∩ E_j (it would satisfy r_i ≤ d(x) < r_i): the E_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets.
5. ((d) Masses.) By ML with U := ℝ^P, E := E_j and V := ℝ^P (the a.e. bound on ξ and the formula of step 3), M(Y_j) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y_j) ≤ μ(E_j ∩ ℝ^P) = μ(E_j); likewise, by ML with E := {d < r_j} and the hypothesis on A_j, M(A_j) ≤ μ({d < r_j}). In particular M(Y_0) ≤ μ(E_0) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) and M(Y_{j+1}) ≤ μ(E_{j+1}) ≤ μ({d < r_j}) because E_{j+1} ⊆ {d < r_j}. This is (d).
6. (Evaluation bound.) Let Z ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) and G ⊆ ℝ^P with M(Z) ≤ μ(G). Then M(Z) ≤ μ(G) < ∞ (μ finite), so EB with U = W := ℝ^P, r := c_ω (tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P, step 1) gives |Z(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(Z).toReal ≤ c_ω·μ(G).toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mono, c_ω ≥ 0).
7. (Summability.) By step 4 and countable additivity (measure_iUnion), Σ_j μ(E_j) = μ(⋃_j E_j) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, so (μ(E_j).toReal)_j is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal). By steps 5 and 6, |Y_j(ω)| ≤ c_ω·μ(E_j).toReal, so (Y_j(ω))_j is summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded).
8. (Partial sums.) By induction on N, Σ_{j=0}^{N} Y_j(ω) = X(ω) − A_N(ω): for N = 0 this is the hypothesis on Y_0, and Σ_{j=0}^{N+1} Y_j(ω) = (X(ω) − A_N(ω)) + (A_N(ω) − A_{N+1}(ω)) = X(ω) − A_{N+1}(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
9. (A_N(ω) → 0.) By steps 5 and 6, |A_N(ω)| ≤ c_ω·μ({d < r_N}).toReal. Since μ({d < r_N}) → 0 and toReal is continuous at 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), c_ω·μ({d < r_N}).toReal → c_ω·0 = 0, so A_N(ω) → 0 (squeeze_zero_norm).
10. ((b) HasSum.) By steps 8 and 9, Σ_{j<N+1} Y_j(ω) = X(ω) − A_N(ω) → X(ω) as N → ∞; shifting the index (tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat 1), the partial sums Σ_{j<N} Y_j(ω) tend to X(ω). As (Y_j(ω))_j is summable (step 7), Summable.hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat gives HasSum (j ↦ Y_j(ω)) (X(ω)). This is (b).
11. (Vanishing lemma.) Since μ(ℝ^P \ spt X) = 0, μ-a.e. x lies in spt X (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem). Let G be Borel, F ⊆ ℝ^P with G ⊆ F, and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt X ∩ F. For μ⌞G-a.e. x we have x ∈ G (ae_restrict_mem) and x ∈ spt X (ae_restrict_of_ae), hence x ∈ spt X ∩ F, x ∉ tsupport ω, ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and f_ω(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence ∫_G f_ω dμ = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
12. ((c) Supports.) spt X is closed by S (ii) and {r_j ≤ d} is closed, so K_j := spt X ∩ {r_j ≤ d} is closed. If tsupport ω is disjoint from K_j, then Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} f_ω dμ = 0 by step 11 with G := E_j ⊆ F := {r_j ≤ d} (step 4); so spt Y_j ⊆ K_j by S (i). If tsupport ω is disjoint from spt X = spt X ∩ ℝ^P, then A_j(ω) = ∫_{d<r_j} f_ω dμ = 0 by step 11 with G := {d < r_j} and F := ℝ^P; so spt A_j ⊆ spt X by S (i) (spt X closed). This is (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Each test form is bounded, |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω, so f_ω = ξ(ω) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, bounded and μ-integrable.
integral_add_compl and setIntegral_sdiff give Y_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ over the half-open shells E_j.
The E_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets; ML gives M(Y_j) ≤ μ(E_j) and M(A_j) ≤ μ({d < r_j}).
EB with ML: |Y_j(ω)| ≤ c_ω μ(E_j) and |A_N(ω)| ≤ c_ω μ({d < r_N}); Σ μ(E_j) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ gives summability.
Partial sums telescope to X(ω) − A_N(ω) → X(ω), hence HasSum.
μ is carried by spt X, so the integrands vanish a.e. when tsupport ω misses spt X ∩ {r_j ≤ d}; S (i), (ii) give the supports.

Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition, with the density estimates of its steps 11(b) and 13(iii); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928) (display (10): ρ ∈ (σ/2, σ) with M⟨T, d, ρ⟩ ≤ (c/σ)·M(T_σ − T_{σ/2})).
1. Put ρ_j := (1/2)^{j+2}. Then ρ_j > 0, ρ_j ≤ (1/2)^2 = 1/4 (pow_le_pow_of_le_one, since j + 2 ≥ 2) and ρ_j/2 = (1/2)^{j+3} (pow_succ).
2. (Choice of r_j; (i) and (vi).) Fix j and put B_j := C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M. By the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ B_j. GR, applied with μ, μ′ (finite), f := d (measurable), ρ := ρ_j > 0 and B := B_j, gives r_j with ρ_j/2 < r_j < ρ_j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ_j)·B_j and liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞. Choose such an r_j for every j (axiom of choice). By step 1 this gives (i), and (vi) holds.
3. ((ii).) For every j, r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j by (i) (applied to j + 1 and to j). Hence r is strictly decreasing (strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt).
4. ((iii).) Since r_j < ρ_j, {d < r_j} ⊆ {d < ρ_j}, so μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M by the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, and ρ_j^{m+2} = ((1/2)^{j+2})^{m+2} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} (pow_mul). The same argument with μ′ and M′ gives the second inequality.
5. ((iv).) Since (j + 2)(m + 2) ≥ j → ∞ and (1/2)^n → 0 (tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one), (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} → 0, hence ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)}) → ofReal 0 = 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). As C ≠ ∞ and M ≠ ∞, C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M → C·0·M = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const). By (iii), 0 ≤ μ({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M, so μ({d < r_j}) → 0 (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le). The same argument with μ′ and M′ ≠ ∞ gives μ′({d < r_j}) → 0.
6. ((v).) For ρ > 0 we have (4/ρ)·ρ^{m+2} = 4ρ^{m+1}, hence ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = ofReal(4ρ^{m+1}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with 4/ρ ≥ 0 and with 4 ≥ 0; ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat). With the liminf bound of step 2 this gives (v). ∎

r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j, so r is strictly decreasing.
μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M (pow_mul), and the same for μ′; this bound tends to 0.

subproblems.title: Boundary mass of the slice of a boundary current by a Lipschitz function
subproblems.statement: Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (SL), the frozen type of Submission.cmc_slice_mass_bounds: for P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), measures μ, μ′ on ℝ^P finite on compact subsets of U, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1} μ-a.e. strongly measurable and ξ′ : ℝ^P → Λ_k μ′-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α for μ-a.e. x and |ξ′(x)(β)| ≤ |β| for all β for μ′-a.e. x, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U), ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ′(x)(η(x)) dμ′(x) for every η ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0), there are A : ℝ → 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and B : ℝ → 𝒟_k(U) with (SL1) A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, (SL2) B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ′(η) dμ′, (SL3) ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η is disjoint from {f = t}, (SL4) M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W (liminf along the filter 𝓝[>] 0, values in [0, ∞]) and (SL5) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for every open W. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U), μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m μ-a.e. strongly measurable such that for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every m-covector α, and assume ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ(x)(η(x)) dμ(x) for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0), t ∈ ℝ, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, and B ∈ 𝒟_m(U) with B(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(x)(η(x)) dμ(x) for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Then boundaryMassOn B W ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) in [0, ∞] (liminf along 𝓝[>] 0; {t − h < f < t} = {x : t − h < f(x) ∧ f(x) < t}). Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.

subproblems.title: boundaryMassOn is subadditive on differences and vanishes on boundaries
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and U, G ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets. Then (a) boundaryMassOn (X − Y) G ≤ boundaryMassOn X G + boundaryMassOn Y G for all X, Y ∈ 𝒟_m(U); and (b) boundaryMassOn (∂X) G = 0 for every X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). 1. (M_G(0) = 0 in every degree.) M_G(0) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal 0(ω) = ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0 over the admissible ω (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply), so M_G(0) ≤ 0 (sSup_le), i.e. M_G(0) = 0.

By MS (with k, U, G, ∂X, ∂Y), M_G(∂(X − Y)) = M_G(∂X − ∂Y) ≤ M_G(∂X) + M_G(∂Y), which is (a).

Adding these bounds (add_le_add) and combining with step 4 gives ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for every admissible ω. By step 1, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). ∎
